title: Software Based Model Development for Design of Area Specific Shelter for Thermal Comfort Maintenance.
description:
• Background:
The ambient atmospheric condition affects the temperature inside the shelter and makes thermal management necessary for maintenance of temperature in the comfortable range. The existing shelters for any region are generally not designed as per the requirements of a particular region and hence not energy efficient thus demands external thermal comfort maintenance system. Area specific designed shelters looks smart and one time solution for thermal management as per the atmospheric condition of the region.
This model development project work is specifically conceptualised keeping in mind the tough climatic condition of High Altitude cold Region like Ladakh and can be used for studying the design requirements of other climatic region shelters as well.
• Description:
The Ladakh region is blessed with high solar energy irradiance (1900-2100 kwh/m2/year) along with long average sunshine duration of 7.9 hours with 300 plus average annual cloud free days. The temperatures inside the shelters found suitable during day hours even during the winter period due to trapping of thermal energy from solar radiation, but approach nearly the ambient atmospheric temperature after sunset. High thermal losses through the material of the shelter and openings contributed towards such low temperature inside shelters.
A detailed thermal analysis of the shelter including size, shape orientation etc.
along with, study related to application of suitable materials and application of thermal mass storage material, composite multi-material etc. and effect of openings on outcome looks to be a potential solution for development of self-sufficient passive shelter for the region in terms of temperature maintenance.
A general model development in ANSYS software to thermally simulate the shelter for study of heat losses and capture of real time atmospheric ambient climatic condition data will prove to be helpful. The project is conceptualised for the development of general model in ANSYS software. The model should be user friendly and works on user defined values (real time data, material properties etc.)to simulate the cases along with comparative analysis with different materials under same ambient condition to predict the most efficient combination of materials, shape, and size etc.in terms of temperature maintenance.
The primary objective of the work/project is to minimize the energy utilisation for thermal comfort maintenance in particular and minimization of fossil fuel application in general by designing of area specific self-sustained standalone passive shelter at defined atmospheric climatic condition.
• Expected Solution:
Development of Software based model for predicating the suitable shelter design including suitable material, size, shape etc. with the objective of thermal comfort maintenance in passive shelter installed in different atmospheric conditions. This work involves simple feeding of collected data and material properties in developed model and outcome shows in terms of most efficient design with materials for thermal comfort maintenance in a particular region The Developed Model should be capable of giving/solving the following tasks:
1. Prediction of shelter inside temperature based on the user defined inputs.
2. Prediction of thermal energy generated from solar radiation.
3. Heat flow details as per the temperature difference between ambient and shelter temperature for a defined time period.
summary: Innovation (2/5): draws on standard software/hardware techniques applied to a agriculture, foodtech & rural development problem, placing it in the incremental band. Feasibility (3/5): as a software build with moderate integration complexity, a full build is tight for 36 hours and will need scope-cutting. Impact (3/5): addresses a more targeted user group within Agriculture, FoodTech & Rural Development. Tech Depth (2/5): centers on model. Sustainability (5/5): has a clear long-term maintenance path. Scalability (3/5): currently scoped narrowly and would need rework to scale. Total 18/30 -> Yellow verdict.

detail.title: Software Model for Area-Specific Shelter Design for Thermal Comfort in High Altitude Cold Regions

overview.in_plain_terms: Build software that models how a shelter's design should change based on the specific climate it's in, so shelters in places like Ladakh actually stay warm at night using their region's abundant sunlight instead of losing all that heat after sunset.
overview.why_it_matters: Ladakh has huge solar potential but current shelters waste it, staying warm by day and freezing by night. A well-designed thermal model directly translates into real energy savings and comfort.
pain_points: Shelters aren't designed for their specific region's climate, leading to energy inefficiency.
High thermal losses through shelter materials mean daytime solar-trapped warmth is lost quickly after sunset.
No systematic software tool exists to model and optimize shelter thermal design for specific regional conditions.
overview.background: Ladakh has abundant solar irradiance and sunshine, and shelters trap useful daytime heat, but poor material/design choices mean high thermal losses cause temperatures to crash after sunset, undermining potential energy efficiency.
overview.whats_being_asked: Software-based modeling for area-specific shelter design that optimizes thermal comfort maintenance based on regional atmospheric/solar conditions, initially for Ladakh but generalizable to other climates.
expected_solution: Thermal modeling software incorporating regional solar irradiance and atmospheric data.
Design optimization for minimizing thermal loss and maximizing solar heat retention.
Generalizable framework applicable to other climatic regions.
Validated improvement over current non-region-specific shelter designs.

analysis.innovation_scope_note: Incremental. Thermal building-performance modeling is an established engineering discipline (building physics simulation), applied here to a specific extreme-climate context.
analysis.invention_effort_note: Low as scored, this is fundamentally a physics-based simulation/modeling software build, achievable using established thermal modeling principles rather than requiring novel invention.

competitive_landscape.note: Niche building-physics simulation PS, few teams will have both the thermal engineering background and interest to engage seriously.

innovation.note: Building thermal performance modeling is an established engineering discipline, applied competently to a specific climate context.

invention.note: A physics-based simulation software build using established heat-transfer principles, not novel invention.

technical_feasibility.note: This is a pure software/simulation task, buildable with publicly available solar irradiance and climate data for Ladakh, no hardware dependency.

impact_and_benefits.note: Genuine energy-efficiency and comfort value for a specific extreme-climate region, with explicit generalizability to other regions.

architecture.note: A physics-based simulation engine with a design-comparison interface, manageable complexity.

overall_verdict.reasoning: Strong pick for a team with building-physics or thermal-engineering background, or willing to research heat-transfer fundamentals. Genuinely achievable in 36 hours as a pure software task, unlike several other DRDO/Ladakh-context PS in this batch that require physical hardware validation.

evaluator_lens.biggest_strength: Pure software task with no hardware dependency, unlike several neighboring PS in this batch, and publicly available solar/climate data for the region exists.
evaluator_lens.biggest_risk: Building a generic thermal simulator without genuinely region-specific solar/climate data grounding would miss the actual point, the value is region-specific optimization, not a generic building physics tool.
evaluator_lens.validate_before_commit: Source real solar irradiance and climate data for Ladakh specifically (the PS provides some figures directly) to ground your model, rather than using generic or placeholder climate assumptions.

idea_0_4: Research basic building thermal physics principles (heat transfer, thermal mass, insulation properties) if not already familiar.
Source Ladakh's actual solar irradiance and temperature data (the PS provides starting figures: 1900-2100 kWh/m2/year, 7.9 hours average sunshine).
Split: one person on the thermal simulation engine, one on the design-comparison/optimization interface.
prototype_4_22: Build the core thermal simulation model incorporating solar gain, material heat-loss properties, and diurnal temperature cycling.
Test the model against the described real-world observation (daytime comfort, post-sunset temperature crash) to confirm it reproduces the actual known problem.
Start the design-optimization layer, testing different material/design choices against the model.
integration_22_30: Connect simulation and optimization into a usable design-comparison tool.
Run several design variations (different insulation, thermal mass, glazing choices) and compare predicted performance.
Test generalizability by running your model against a different climate profile to confirm the framework isn't Ladakh-only.
polish_30_36: Build a clear visualization comparing baseline shelter design against your optimized design's predicted thermal performance over a full day-night cycle.
Rehearse walking through your model's physics basis and how it matches the real described problem (daytime warmth, post-sunset crash).
Prepare to discuss generalizability to other climatic regions explicitly, as the PS requests.
build_plan.how_to_stand_out: Show your model correctly reproducing the real described phenomenon (good daytime comfort, crashing post-sunset temperatures) for a baseline design, then show your optimized design maintaining comfort through the night, that before/after simulation result is the actual deliverable.

strengths: Pure software task with no hardware dependency, genuinely achievable in 36 hours unlike several neighboring PS.
Real regional climate data is available and cited directly in the problem statement.
weaknesses: Requires genuine building-physics/thermal-engineering understanding to model correctly, not a trivial software build.
Lower innovation ceiling than some flashier PS, differentiation depends on modeling accuracy and design-optimization quality.

team_fit.ideal_ratio: Weight toward genuine thermal-physics understanding, this is the actual technical core of the PS.
team_fit.approach: Research basic building thermal physics fundamentals early if the team isn't already familiar, incorrect physics undermines the entire model's credibility.

ai_buildability_split.ai_can_build_fast: The simulation engine scaffolding (heat-transfer equations are well-documented) and the visualization/comparison UI.
ai_buildability_split.needs_human_judgment: Correctly applying and validating the thermal physics for this specific extreme climate context, and interpreting whether the model's output is physically plausible, that's engineering judgment.
ai_buildability_split.risk_of_leaning_on_ai_only: An AI-generated thermal model with subtly incorrect physics could produce plausible-looking but wrong design recommendations, validate against the real described phenomenon (daytime warmth, post-sunset crash) as a sanity check.

data_resource_availability.status: Real Ladakh solar irradiance and climate data is publicly available and partially provided directly in the PS text, one of the better-resourced PS in the batch for real data access.
data_resource_availability.backup_plan: Not needed, real data access is genuinely available here.

judge_qna.question: How do you know your thermal model's physics are actually correct, not just plausible-looking?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Show your model reproducing the real, described phenomenon (daytime comfort due to solar trapping, rapid post-sunset temperature crash) as a validation check, if it matches known real behavior, that's evidence the underlying physics is sound.
judge_qna.follow_up: What thermal physics principles specifically are you modeling, conduction, convection, radiation, thermal mass?

judge_qna.question: How would this generalize to a completely different climate, say a hot, humid region?
judge_qna.strong_answer: Walk through how your model's core physics engine is climate-agnostic, only the input parameters (solar irradiance, temperature profile, humidity) change, demonstrating this with a second test case if you built one.
judge_qna.follow_up: What design factors would completely reverse for a hot climate versus this cold-climate optimization?
